thread:
Priya R: FYI - saw a customer hit a regional surge and the console suggested a 'cheap swap' that actually increased their token spend. Can we look into the heuristic? :thinking_face:
Matt H: ugh. do we have the logs / example request? which policy did the console pick?
Priya R: app id cst-552, region eu-west-1. Console UI highlighted economy-v2 as a lower-latency, cheaper option. They switched and then usage spiked because messages were longer and economy-v2 has softer truncation -> more tokens.
Jess: that's a UX problem too — the callout says "lower cost" but doesn't surface token/length tradeoffs. We should show an estimated token delta and sample output length.
Sam: agree. On routing side, our current scoring is: score = latency_weight * est_latency + cost_weight * est_model_cost. We don't include expected token amplification for that model.
Matt H: right now est_model_cost is a per-token estimate from profile, but it assumes similar output length. We need an estimator: est_tokens_out(model, prompt) -> expected multiplier.
Priya R: can we do a quick mitigation? Prefer not to auto-suggest economy-v2 for "standard" tier when expected token delta > 15% unless user explicitly opts in.
Matt H: implementable. Quick config sketch for the policy:```yaml
policy_name: prefer-economy-with-guardrails
target_tiers: [standard, free]
prefer_variants: [economy-v2]
max_expected_output_delta_pct: 15
token_budget_control:
  per_request_max_tokens: null
  per_minute_budget: 100000
```
Jess: on the console, instead of just a green badge, show: "Estimated tokens: +18% -> projected cost +10%" with a tooltip "based on sample prompts and telemetry". Also add an "Explain" link that shows sample outputs.
Sam: telemetry question — do we have per-variant output length histograms by region and customer tier? billing-bot: [auto] pulled usage histograms for economy-v2 vs base in eu-west-1 for last 30d: median_out_tokens: base=42, economy-v2=52, p95_out_tokens: base=180, economy-v2=220.
Priya R: ok those numbers explain it. For rollout UX: default to "suggest" not "recommend" for low tiers and add an opt-out toggle in Preferences.
Matt H: technical plan: (1) add estimator service that returns expected_output_multiplier given model, prompt fingerprint, region; (2) update routing policy evaluation to multiply est_model_cost by multiplier; (3) surface prospective delta in console. I can spike (1) in a week.
Jess: I'll update the UI mocks to show the delta and a small explainer card. We'll need an API from estimator:```json
{ "model": "economy-v2", "region": "eu-west-1", "prompt_sample_hash": "abc123" }
// response: { "expected_multiplier": 1.18, "confidence": 0.6 }
```
Sam: for safety, add a quick simulator endpoint so ops can run a batch on a small prompt set to get expected cost change before apply. Recommend a dry-run flag in rollout API.
Priya R: can we also gate by token budget? if a customer has a monthly token budget and switching pushes them past 90% projected, don't suggest.
Matt H: yep — add a budget check hook. We'll need a cheap cache per-customer to avoid re-evaluating on every request.
Jess: UX note: for the toggle label use "Allow cost-optimizations (may change outputs)" and tooltip linking to docs.
Sam: I'll add an observability dashboard tile: per-variant token-multiplier heatmap by region and tier + alerts if projected monthly spend delta > 5% after rollout.
Priya R: nice. Timeline? Matt, spike in 7 days. Jess and Sam sync with Matt mid-week. I'll draft copy for the console.
Matt H: 👍 starting spike Monday. Will post RFC when I have the estimator proto.
Priya R: thanks all :thumbsup:
Jess: created a quick ticket and linked the mock: https://redwood.internal/ops/tickets/PLAT-1029
Sam: added a prometheus metric proposal to the ticket (plat.routing.expected_token_multiplier)
billing-bot: [auto] created alert: routing-projected-spend-delta (>5%) for env=prod.
